extracted.intended_audience: researchers and academics invited or seeking to act as peer reviewers for Sage journals (including first-time/inexperienced reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting peer review of journal manuscript submissions for Sage journals, covering reviewer responsibilities, practical steps before and during a review, and how to make and justify editorial recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing / meeting deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform the editor immediately if you will not be able to meet the deadline and keep your availability updated in Sage Track to avoid receiving invitations to review when you are unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify the editor as soon as possible if you cannot accept or will miss a deadline. If you cannot review a manuscript, suggest an alternative reviewer to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability / conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you have any reason why you should not review the submission? If in doubt, check with the journal’s editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the manuscript falls within your expertise and whether any conflicts of interest exist. Consult the journal editor if unsure and learn more about your ethical responsibilities as a reviewer (see Ethics and Responsibility/COPE guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not share the content of a paper you have been invited to review, unless you have permission from the journal’s editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain strict confidentiality of manuscript content. If you suspect author misconduct, discuss concerns only with the editor rather than sharing manuscript details more widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co‑reviewing / involving colleagues or students
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform the journal editor if you wish to collaborate on a review with a colleague or student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get editor approval before co-reviewing and follow the journal's/COPE's guidance on co-reviewing. Where applicable, co-reviewers can receive credit (e.g., via Web of Science Reviewer Recognition) but the editor must be informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow individual journal reviewer guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals ask reviewers to answer specific questions, so check what is expected before beginning your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before starting, review the journal-specific reviewer form/questions and any journal guidance to ensure you address the required items and structure your report accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to include in a review (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the manuscript and include review comments for authors and (where applicable) confidential comments for the editor. Sage offers a step‑by‑step video walkthrough and written instructions on how to assess a manuscript and what to include in a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover the manuscript’s validity, originality, clarity, methodology, analysis, interpretation and contribution; provide clear, constructive, and actionable comments. Use available Sage resources (video/tutorials/downloadable instructions) for structure and example phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: Accept
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept: No further revision required. The manuscript is publishable in its current form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is uncommon; majority of articles require revision. Only recommend Accept when the manuscript requires no corrections or clarifications and meets journal standards for quality and contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: Minor Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor Revision: The paper is mostly sound but will be sent back to the authors for minor corrections and clarifications such as the addition of minor citations or the tweaking of arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These revisions should not involve any major changes. Changes should be clearly marked for the attention of the previous reviewers. The paper may be subject to re‑review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: Major Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Major Revision: The principle of the article is sound and it has a chance of being accepted but requires substantial change to be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial changes may include further experiments or analysis, inclusion of additional literature or theory, or improvement of arguments and conclusions. Authors are required to submit a point‑by‑point response to the reviewers and the paper will be subject to a re‑review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: Reject
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject: The manuscript is of insufficient quality, novelty or significance to warrant publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issues of quality, novelty and/or contribution cannot be addressed through revision, recommend rejection rather than revision. Editors may still reject papers if revisions are insufficient. Even when recommending rejection, provide suggestions for improvement in the Comments to the Authors field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess novelty and contribution against journal expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the journal Aims and Scope for any specific requirements with regard to levels of novelty and/or contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging novelty/significance, align your assessment with the journal’s stated aims and scope. If the manuscript’s novelty or contribution is borderline, indicate this and reference the journal’s standards where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive feedback regardless of recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when recommending rejection, the reviewer is encouraged to share their suggestions for improvement in the Comments to the Authors field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame critiques constructively and, where possible, give actionable suggestions to improve quality, clarity, and rigour so authors can revise or submit elsewhere with guidance.
